newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices gain on more export news.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices gain on more export news.

text.p: Indian cotton prices gained on Tuesday after the government said it was allowing further cotton exports of 345,000 bales (170 kg each) for the new season starting this month, traders said.
Last week, the government allowed export of 150,000 bales.
"After a short interval, the government has allowed more exports. This triggered some speculative activity," one trader said. In 1995/96 season, 1.65 million bales were allowed.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees to 835/870 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned moved up by 15 rupees to 1,625/1,670. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose by 100 rupees to 12,500/12,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
